tips.title: Collège is not college
tips.body: **Le collège** is the school for ages 11 to 15 — the equivalent of Years 7 to 10. **Le lycée** is 15 to 18. A French *collège* is nothing like an English college, and translating it that way is the classic false friend in this topic.

tips.title: The years count down
tips.body: *La **sixième*** is the **first** year of collège, then *la cinquième, la quatrième, la troisième*. They count down towards the exam year, then the lycée restarts at *la seconde, la première, la terminale*. An English Year 9 student is in *la quatrième*.

tips.title: Marks are out of 20
tips.body: *J'ai eu **quinze sur vingt**.* French marks run 0 to 20, and **10 sur 20** is the pass. *Quinze* is a good mark, *dix-huit* is excellent. Writing a percentage instead is an English habit that reads as untranslated.

tips.title: Le bac at the end
tips.body: **Le baccalauréat** (*le bac*) is the exam at the end of the *lycée*, at 18 — the rough equivalent of A levels, not GCSEs. *Le brevet* is the exam at the end of the *collège*, and that is the one nearer to GCSEs.

tips.title: Pas de cours le mercredi après-midi
tips.body: In many French schools there are **no lessons on Wednesday afternoon**, and the day is longer to make up for it — often 8h to 17h with a two-hour lunch. Days, length and the Wednesday gap are the three facts a comparison question wants.

steps.title: Le système scolaire
steps.body:
A French school career runs through three schools, and each has its own name.

**L'école primaire** — ages 6 to 11. **Le collège** — ages 11 to 15. **Le lycée** — ages 15 to 18.

**Le collège** is where a British Year 7 to Year 10 student would be, and its years count **down**: *la sixième* (Year 7), *la cinquième* (Year 8), *la quatrième* (Year 9), *la troisième* (Year 10). At the end comes **le brevet**, the exam closest to GCSEs.

**Le lycée** then runs *la seconde, la première, la terminale*, ending in **le baccalauréat** — *le bac* — at 18.

**Saying where you are**: *je suis **en** quatrième* (I am in Year 9), *je vais **au** collège*, *mon collège s'appelle …*, *je suis élève dans un collège mixte* (mixed).

**Kinds of school**: *une école publique* (state), *une école privée*, *un internat* (boarding school), *un collège mixte*, *une école pour filles / garçons*.

**People**: *un(e) élève* (pupil), *un(e) prof* (*un professeur*), *le directeur / la directrice* (head), *un(e) surveillant(e)* (supervisor), *le CPE* (the member of staff who deals with discipline and attendance).

steps.title: La journée scolaire
steps.body:
The **school day** is one of the biggest differences, and the exam asks about it constantly.

**Times**: *les cours commencent à huit heures et finissent à dix-sept heures* — 8h to 17h. With a lunch break of 2 hours that is 7 hours of lessons.

**The Wednesday gap**: *le mercredi après-midi, il n'y a pas de cours* — no lessons on Wednesday afternoon in many schools. Some schools have lessons on Saturday morning instead.

**Lunch**: *la pause déjeuner dure deux heures* (lasts two hours), *on mange à la cantine* (canteen), *un repas chaud avec une entrée, un plat et un dessert* (starter, main, dessert).

**Lessons**: *un cours dure cinquante-cinq minutes*, *on a huit cours par jour*, *la récréation* (break), *l'emploi du temps* (timetable), *une heure d'étude* (a study period).

**Marks**: *les notes sont sur 20*. *10 sur 20* is the pass, *15 sur 20* a good mark. *Un bulletin scolaire* is the report; *redoubler* is to repeat the year, which happens in France and almost never in England.

**Uniform**: *en France, on ne porte pas d'uniforme* — a fact almost every comparison question uses.

steps.title: Le collège ailleurs dans le monde francophone
steps.body:
French is spoken far beyond France, and school life differs across the **Francophone world** — a comparison a reading text may set up.

**Au Sénégal**: *le français est la langue de l'école*, but pupils also speak *le wolof* at home. *Les classes sont souvent grandes* — classes of forty or more are common. *Beaucoup d'élèves marchent longtemps pour aller à l'école.*

**Au Québec**: *l'école secondaire* runs from 12 to 17, then *le cégep* before university. *Les cours sont en français* in most schools, and there is a law protecting French.

**En Belgique et en Suisse**: the systems are close to the French one, with *l'école secondaire* and marks out of 20 or 10 depending on the region.

**Useful comparison language**: *en France … tandis qu'au Sénégal …* (whereas), *par rapport à* (compared to), *le même système que* (the same system as), *la différence principale, c'est que …*, *ce qui m'étonne, c'est que …* (what surprises me is that).

**Access to school**: *tous les enfants n'ont pas accès à l'éducation* (not all children have access), *certains doivent travailler*, *l'éducation est un droit* (a right), *apprendre à lire et à écrire* (learn to read and write).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Name the three French schools and the ages each covers.
2. Which French year matches Year 7, Year 9 and Year 10?
3. Write *a mark out of twenty* and say what the pass mark is.

**Part B.**

4. Describe the French school day: start, finish, lunch, Wednesday.
5. Write two differences between France and England, using *par contre*.
6. Write *in France you can repeat the year*.

**Part C.**

7. Write a sentence comparing France with another Francophone country, using *tandis que*.
8. Give your opinion of the French system with a reason.
9. Write six sentences comparing school in France with school here, with at least three differences and a judgement.

For question 9, name the French fact before you judge it.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Use the French words, not translations.** *Le collège, le lycée, la quatrième, le brevet, le bac, la cantine, l'emploi du temps.* Writing *college* for *collège* or *A levels* for *le bac* loses the mark and shows you have not learnt the system.

**Know the year names cold.** *Sixième, cinquième, quatrième, troisième* then *seconde, première, terminale*. A listening text will say one and expect you to know the age.

**Marks out of 20.** *J'ai eu seize sur vingt* — and *10 sur 20* is the pass. Percentages are not how French schools report.

**Contrast properly.** *Par contre, tandis que, alors que, par rapport à, en revanche.* A comparison built on *mais* alone reads as Year 7; these connectives are what the top band sounds like.

**Use ce qui and ce que.** *Ce qui m'étonne, c'est la longueur de la journée. Ce que je préfère, c'est l'absence d'uniforme.* Fronting the idea is a complex structure examiners notice.

**Judge, do not just list.** *Le système français est plus strict, mais je pense que les repas sont meilleurs.* **Meilleur** is the comparative of *bon* — never *plus bon*.

**Bring in the wider Francophone world.** One sentence about Senegal or Quebec shows cultural knowledge, which the mark scheme rewards separately from language.

**Do not overstate.** *Dans beaucoup d'écoles françaises* is safer than *en France, toutes les écoles…* — and hedging accurately is itself a higher-band skill.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body: - **L'école primaire** (6–11), **le collège** (11–15), **le lycée** (15–18). - Collège years count down: *la sixième, la cinquième, la quatrième, la troisième*. - Lycée: *la seconde, la première, la terminale*. - **Le brevet** at the end of collège, **le bac** at the end of lycée. - *Je suis **en** quatrième; je vais **au** collège.* - Day: about **8h to 17h**, a **2-hour** lunch, often **no lessons on Wednesday afternoon**. - *Un cours dure cinquante-cinq minutes; la récréation; l'emploi du temps.* - Marks are **sur 20**; *10 sur 20* is the pass; *redoubler* is to repeat the year. - *En France, on ne porte pas d'uniforme.* - Contrast with *par contre, tandis que, alors que, en revanche, par rapport à*. - *Meilleur*, not *plus bon*. - Front an idea with *ce qui / ce que … c'est …* - Elsewhere: *le Sénégal, le Québec* (*le cégep*), *la Belgique*.

examTechnique.body:
Use the French terms — *le collège, le lycée, la quatrième, le brevet, le bac, la cantine* — and never translate *collège* as college. Know the year names, the 8h–17h day, the Wednesday afternoon, marks **sur 20**, *redoubler* and the absence of uniform.

Contrast with *par contre, tandis que, en revanche*, judge with *plus … que* and **meilleur**, front an idea with *ce qui / ce que … c'est …*, and add one fact about the wider Francophone world.
examinerErrors: Confusing le brevet with le bac.
Keeping un after a negative — pas un uniforme.
Claiming every French school is the same.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer uses the French terms precisely, places a pupil in the right year, and quotes the day, the marks and the Wednesday afternoon accurately. It contrasts with *tandis que* and *en revanche* rather than repeating *mais*, judges with *plus … que* and *meilleur*, fronts an idea with *ce qui m'étonne, c'est que…*, hedges its claims with *dans beaucoup d'écoles*, and brings in Senegal or Quebec for cultural range.
